what: On a trial's Changes tab, a person who scrolls down and clicks Mark reviewed before the watchlist's list of trials to review has loaded is thrown back to the top of the page when that list arrives, losing their place; a person who only scrolls down to read is thrown back the same way. The spec's rule that marking reviewed holds the scroll is broken in that moment. This build makes the moment more inviting, because the review bar now looks complete before the list arrives; on a local machine the list usually arrives within a fraction of a second, so I do not know how often a person meets it. I ran it with the list held back: the page was scrolled to 381 (1440 x 900) and 745 (1024 x 768) after marking, and to 0 once the list arrived, at both window sizes. The reviewer found the same fault as review-trial-page-01; this adds the Mark reviewed case. The cause is that the router scrolls to the top only after the trial page has finished drawing, and the trial page finishes only after the list has answered.

When a trial is open in two browser tabs and its changes are marked reviewed in one, clicking Mark reviewed in the other says "5 changes marked reviewed" and offers Undo, and that Undo shows the program error "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'id')" and undoes nothing. This was not changed by this build; the same error after a double click was fixed earlier (E-033), but not this way of reaching it. The cause is that the server answers a review of changes already reviewed with no review to undo, and the page builds an Undo for it anyway.

When the watchlist's list of trials to review fails to load, the trial page turns Next trial off and its hover text says "No other trial needs review", which may be untrue, and nothing on the page says the list failed. This was not changed by this build, but the build now shows the button as waiting until that answer, so it is the only thing a person sees. I am unsure how much this matters, since the text appears only on hover; the fixer may judge it not a defect. The cause is that the page treats a failed answer as an empty list.
